*refugi, clima i barri*
/
Montjuïc is more than an emblematic mountain within the urban fabric of Barcelona; it is the summit that has witnessed its historical evolution. In this context, this intervention is located between two significant mountain climbs.

The appearance of the ‘mountain refuge’ is proposed, activating a space that favors contemplation and encounter, in a crowded placeof history, such as Casaramona or the Mies pavilion, and monumentality but with a look towards the neighbourhood and its people. The project also includes the transformation of the façade of Hall 8, making it more permeable and inviting interaction, while reinforcing the expression of the architectural proposal.

*Matosinhos, Porto*
Taller Belén Ramos
Three workshop houses for artists
/
The sculptor eagerly recognized the house that Souto de Moura had had built decades ago. When he came across the estate where he would spend the next few summers, everything seemed scattered, as if they had been putting together pieces of walls, of roofs, of empty spaces and of orchards, picking them up one by one, as if mounting a wall with found stones. But little by little, with each alignment, with each new wall raised,a modulated volumes compass was discovered, recognizing the dynamic character of the narrow streets, roofs and boats of Matosinhos. The concrete walls seen, almost like hundred-year-old statues, showed the scars that the rainwater had been leaving, while the upper part was deformed to become an open channel, distributing the torrent of zinc roofs towards the orchards and the border forest. He was surprisedbeing received by an outdoor space that, without funnels, showed the door of the workshop where he would create his new collection. Through a gap, a distributor courtyard opened, a modern cloister, which gave access to the rest rooms of the estate. As if he had never left the narrow streets of Matosinhos, he was now discovering a small town that, without realizing it, would become homehis.

Arriving at a well-lit room, he settled in, before moving on to the living room. In that courtyard protected by walls, I already saw summer lunches with company. A discreet kitchen accompanied the space with a board that crossed the load-bearing wall, communicating with the exterior courtyard. The sculptor went to the last room. The workshop was wide and wasdrawn between two concrete wallss. He appreciated the texture of the formwork once inside.

This border was crossed by a large sliding door, made of sheet metal and memories of the industrial port, which he had to push hard. Once the threshold was crossed, a small era unfolded, flanked by the old orchardss that were drawn between the two walls. As he contemplated that scenario, hesurprise the cry of his new neighbor, a writer immersed in his novel, who also seemed captivated by the place. He insisted on recording the first impressions that this architecture had awakened in him.

6afe966b4009bc151c73bd21b1a8b127d9fb6e65:
*Vestuari a la platja de la Barceloneta*
Taller Carme Ribas & Miquel Mariner, $el tercer temps$
/
The project invites you to find a hidden shell in the plenum. An artifice . The void that a body generates when it wrinkles is filled with a paste that dries with a clear gravitational impact. These pieces, as soon as they are strategically grouped, will become the hollow of a shell, a wrapper that wraps them up. Two incisions cut out this thin film, which gives a glimpse of an input filter anddeparture in what will be a new wardrobe for the beach. A ritual of what is naked, dressed, and finally completely undressed. The change of scale allows a generating body to close a space where human bodies hide, breathe, wipe, enter and exit. The unit of measurement remains what lies between two hands or two feet.

*Es Molinar, Palma de Mallorca*
Taller Arnau Sastre, $hcc etsab$
/
A repetition of steel trusses crosses the entire plot and becomes a white canvas that the project takes as a starting point. On this support, the space is not filled homogeneously, but is stressed in gravities: elements that attract uses and looks. 

These devices appear in contact with the border built in the interior of the island, increasing the potential of the oldcourtyards of stone, and also within the new dwellings, exploring new ways of programming and deprogramming such stays. The courtyards of floor plan Baja act as filters of ventilation and intimacy, while the modules that open towards the interior of the island transform this level into a space for meeting, exhibition and coexistence, where daily life is amplified as a collective event.

However, what really moves him is the dance. Dancing from an early age, it's both a haven and a way to connect with the space. When she dances, everything fits: the body, the air, the silence. It is another way of communicating, more sincere than any word.

*Boavista, Porto*
Taller Belén Ramos
/
workshop office complex in Porto. 
In the past, a factory complex was the protagonist of a terrain between fields and some small urban centres. Over decades, this area has been gradually built with varied uses, occupying green spaces that the rain had irrigated, and hiding streams that were previously part of the sonority of the urban landscape.

The topography configures the site as an open aquifernatural. The complex is located in such a way that it is protected from possible flooding; the new channel is both a road and a barrier. The water collected by the roofs system is channeled through downspouts until it returns to the channel. In this way, the water cycle is closed and the footprint of the new construction is minimized.

6e50f04c45d57568cc0a656c16a0ba61a403a576:
*Vestuari a la platja de la Barceloneta*
Taller Carme Ribas & Miquel Mariner, $el tercer temps$
/
The project invites you to find a shell hidden inside the plenum. The cavities that are formed when the body is wrinkled are filled with a modelling paste that, when dried, fixes the footprints and irregularities of the body, under the impact of gravity. These pieces, born directly from the body, are strategically grouped to form a set that is wrapped with maixé paper. The shell isfolds up and turns what was full into an inner void.

Two incisions pierce this thin film and make the void accessible: an entrance and an exit that transform the shell into a beach wardrobe. Go in naked, hide, breathe, dry off, get dressed and come out again. The change of scale converts a generating body into an architecture capable of accommodating other bodies, such as asmall grotto or shelter. The unit of measurement, however, continues to be that of the body: what remains between two hands, between two feet, between two parts that come together and that, when separated, build a space.

The resulting pieces are grouped and wrapped with papier-mâché, building a thin shell that transforms the whole into a void. Two incisions pierce it and make this interior accessible:an entrance and an exit that turn the shell into a beach wardrobe. Going in naked, hiding, breathing, wiping, dressing, and going out. A body that, changing scale, becomes architecture and welcomes other bodies. The measurement continues to be that of the body: the space between two hands, between two feet.
